newsitem.title: USA: Dole blasts Clinton foreign policy.
newsitem.headline: Dole blasts Clinton foreign policy.

text.p: Republican presidential candidate Bob Dole blasted President Bill Clinton's foreign policy as "rudderless and illusionary" on Thursday and suggested Clinton may have convened the inconclusive Middle East summit to help get re-elected.

In one of his longest and most detailed speeches yet on foreign policy, Dole charged Clinton squandered American power from Bosnia to Northern Ireland, with major failures in Northern Iraq and Haiti as well.
"(The) Clinton administration's foreign policy is rudderless and illusionary," Dole said.

"In the last three years you and I have seen a series of photo opportunities, treaty signings, staged handshakes and even military theatrics -- all designed to create the impression of foreign policy progress," Dole told a meeting of businessmen in this east Tennessee city.

The White House responded by claiming that Dole himself largely agreed with the administration's handling of foreign policy and suggested the Republican candidate was echoing the perspective of his advisers.
"They are nattering naysayers of gloom," declared White House spokesman Mike McCurry.

"The world is in a better position than it was four years ago because of the conduct of U.S. foreign policy and the very truth of the matter is that Bob Dole, largely spoken, doesn't fundamentally disagree with this position," he said.
Dole called the just-concluded summit between Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, Palestinian President Yasser Arafat and Jordan's King Hussein "hastily convened."

"Frankly it is unclear what President Clinton expected out of a such a meeting. Some have suggested he may have had November 5 (the date of the presidential election) on his mind." Netanyahu and Arafat returned to the Middle East having failed to resolve their differences but they pledged further talks.
Dole said the Clinton administration had repeatedly failed on the world stage.
"It is painful to recall but this is how Clinton has squandered American power," he said.

First, Dole said, the Clinton administration neglected or was indecisive about foreign crises, then made idle threats and concessions in a bid to capture headlines. "Finally, victory is declared, no matter how obvious the failure," he said.
"This is not foreign relations, this is public relations. It does not defuse problems or even confront them. It merely postpones and deepens their worst consequences.
"It sacrifices enduring American interests to the White House's short-term political fixes ... Friends no longer respect us, enemies no longer fear us."

Dole met with Israeli leader Netanyahu on Wednesday night and spent part of the morning discussing foreign policy with key advisers including Colin Powell, the retired chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff.

Dole was scathing about the Clinton administration's policies in Iraq, saying "Saddam Hussein is better off now that he was four years ago" because Clinton neglected the anti-Saddam coalition and growing tensions among the Kurds. He accused Clinton of abandoning the Kurdish safe havens established by the United States.
He said Clinton squandered $3 billion to restore "a democracy that never was" in Haiti and said death squads were once again roaming that country's streets.
"I will pursue a strategy for success," he said, by following American interests around the world and never surrendering any power to the United Nations.
